mutants.label: single-copy-fast-path-removed
mutants.why: A key seen once goes through the merge loop instead: merged = dict(group[0]), and every non-key column has at most one distinct value, so merged[column] is that value (or None when it was None) -- the output record equals group[0] by value, column for column, with NaN preserved. The fast path is a pure optimisation (it skips a dict copy and the per-column scan); the only difference is object identity of the dict, which _frame_for never reads. Inert over every input shape the loaders build; it would stop being inert only if a record carried a column _collapse_by_key's merged dict does not (it copies group[0], so it cannot).

mutants.label: collapse-inside-transaction-after-delete
mutants.why: The except clause rolls the transaction back and re-raises, and DuckDB's rollback restores the deleted rows, so on a conflict the table, the exception and the connection are all identical to the real order; the only difference is that the transaction is held open (and the delete issued) for the duration of the pure-Python collapse. Inert over every state a single-connection test can observe. It would matter only to a concurrent writer or to an observer of the write-ahead log, neither of which this suite has. The distinct hazard -- the collapse raising after `begin transaction` but outside the try, which leaves the transaction OPEN -- is its own row below.
